Cube Clubhouse™ COPPA Facts

What Cube Clubhouse does, and does not do, with children’s information. COPPA is the US law that protects the privacy of children under 13.

Who the app is for

Cube Clubhouse is made for anyone aged 6 and over, and children use it. So it is built as if every person who opens it might be a child: it collects nothing from anyone, and it makes no internet request at all.

The facts

  • Nothing is collected

    There are no accounts, sign-ins, forms, chat or boxes to type words into. Stars, times and settings stay on the device and are never sent to us or anyone else.

  • No identifiers, and no internet requests

    The app makes and reads no identifier: no advertising identifier, no vendor identifier, no device ID, no cookies. It makes no internet request of any kind, not even to look for a new version; new versions come through the App Store.

  • No third-party code

    There is no advertising, analytics, crash reporting, social buttons or software kits. The app sends nothing to anyone, Apple included.

  • Nothing shared

    Nothing is collected, so nothing is shared, sold or disclosed to anyone.

  • A privacy page one tap away

    The Privacy page is one tap from every screen (Privacy, at the bottom) and is published in the same words for the App Store listing. It names us and how to reach us, lists everything the app keeps and where, says how long anything is kept, and explains a parent’s choices.

  • No notice to send, no consent to ask for

    Because no child’s information is collected, the app sends no notice to parents and asks for no consent.

  • If a child writes to us

    The app has no email link, and asks children to have a grown-up write for them. If a child writes anyway, we answer once, asking a grown-up to write instead, and delete the message and the address no later than 7 days after it arrives. A child’s address is never added to any list.

  • Parents can delete everything

    We hold nothing about any child. Everything the app keeps is on the device: Clear Saved Progress on the About page, or deleting the app, erases it. A grown-up who has written to us can ask us to delete the message, and we will.

  • Nothing asked in order to play

    Every lesson, puzzle and tool works without giving any information at all.

  • Keeping information safe

    There is no children’s information for us to hold. Our support mailbox is protected with a strong password and two-step verification, and only Ira Learning LLC reads it. Every build of the app is checked automatically for anything that would collect or send information.

  • How long anything is kept

    On the device: until it is cleared or the app is deleted. A grown-up’s email: until we have finished helping, and no later than 12 months after the last message. A child’s email: no later than 7 days after it arrives.

  • Everyone treated as possibly a child

    The app does not ask anyone’s age. It treats every person as possibly a child, so it needs no age screen.

  • No links out, and no shop

    There are no links that leave the app, and the app refuses to open one. There are no purchases and no way to reach the App Store from inside the app.

What we do, as the publisher

  • Keep the support mailbox, support@iralearningllc.com, working, and check it at least once a week.
  • Protect it with a strong, unique password and two-step verification.
  • Answer a child once, asking a grown-up to write, and delete the child’s message within 7 days.
  • Delete a grown-up’s messages once we have finished helping, and no later than 12 months after the last one.
  • Never add anyone’s address, least of all a child’s, to a mailing list or any other list.
  • Look over the app again every year, and before any version that changes what it does with information.
